properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.77.0): every door call is recorded as client "reflow2-mcp --call", because the in-process client hardcodes that name. And none of the three routes reflow2 has for naming the acting agent can be reached through the door: request _meta cannot be set by --args, writes_for lasts one session and each call is a new session (a new seat), and the client-name match sees the fixed string
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, triage agent B. Item L10 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02: "Telemetry can't name the harness. Every call identifies as `reflow2-mcp --call`."

② PRECEDENT: already recorded as limitation 10 in fact:field-report-vscode-copilot-with-mcp-blocked-reaches-reflow2-only-through-the-call-door-2026-10-01 (client name main.rs:722). The MUST "door calls can be attributed to the product that made them" is in req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current, idea 8 (settled under dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp).

⑤ MEASURED (14 door calls on a scratch store, then `--call usage_report`):
- environment.harness_last_connected = "reflow2-mcp --call 0.77.0"; tally.clients = {"reflow2-mcp --call 0.77.0": 14}.
- Each ledger line (<store>.usage.jsonl) carries client "reflow2-mcp --call" and client_version 0.77.0, plus a seat that DIFFERS on every call (host:pid:nonce).
- Code (origin/main 66620f7): OneShotClient::get_info sets the name literally (main.rs:722), and there is no REFLOW2_HARNESS or flag anywhere in crates/.
- The acting-agent resolver effective_acting_agent (service.rs ~7039) tries three routes in order:
  - request `_meta["reflow2/acting_agent"]`: the door builds CallToolRequestParams from --args alone, so it cannot carry _meta;
  - the session's writes_for acting_agent: lost, because every call is a fresh session;
  - an automated_agent Contributor whose handle equals the client name: the fixed string, so one such Contributor would claim every door call from every harness.

⑥ CLASS: the door was built for builds (cap:a-build-can-call-one-tool-from-the-shell-and-read-the-reply-as-json), where "the door" was a sufficient name. Becoming a supported harness widened who calls it, and nothing that identifies a caller was widened with it. The fix the requirement names (an env or flag on the client name) also gives the third attribution route a real key. The first two need a per-call argument, or the door joining a session (another slice).

CONFIRMED.
